role.altitude: The clinical research coordinator keeps informing patients, collecting adverse events, conferring with investigators and overseeing consent; copying values into case report forms, tracking visit windows and deadlines by hand and re-entering enrolments shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking proposed form values against source documents
Running the study from deadline and visit-window lists
role.ambitious_version: A coordinator who never misses a reporting deadline or visit window and spends the time with patients.

tasks.short: Prepare with the approved patient information, inform patients or caregivers about study aspects and outcomes to be expected, answer their follow-up questions and record the information given.

steps.what: Clinical research coordinator prepares the conversation with the approved patient information
Clinical research coordinator informs patients or caregivers about study aspects and outcomes to be expected
Clinical research coordinator answers follow-up questions by phone or mail
Clinical research coordinator records the information given and its version in the study file

tasks.design: Conversations with patients stay fully human. The coordinator keeps an internal question list per study built from the approved patient information, which speeds answers to follow-up questions. The coordinator still records which information version was given and when in the study file; this first record keeps its time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers and notes were written from scratch each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic study files with checklists and version control.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who hope for more than a study can offer.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining uncertainty honestly to a worried patient.

evidence.claim: A policy tool keeps a versioned document library with approvals.

assumptions: Boundary: informing patients about a study; consent is a separate task.
The question list quotes only the approved patient information; anything else goes to the investigator.

Conversations keep their full or nearly full time; s3 keeps 90 because answers are found in the question list instead of the full document. Recording the information given (s4) is a first record and keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do patients ask fewer repeat questions?

incremental.description: Clinical research coordinator keeps the question list current with amendments.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: patients ask questions the list does not cover, so answering keeps its full time and only preparation is quicker (1.9); high: the question list covers most follow-up questions as designed (4.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect and record adverse event and side effect data, enter it in the case report form, confer with investigators regarding the reporting of events, prepare the report, have it signed, submit it to oversight agencies and track deadlines.

steps.what: Clinical research coordinator collects adverse event and side effect information from the patient and records
Clinical research coordinator enters adverse event data in the case report form

loop.input: Source documents from the medical record for the event.
loop.output: Proposed values for the adverse event form fields, each linked to its source passage.
loop.check: The coordinator checks that the linked source passage really supports each proposed value (the event, its start and end dates, grade and outcome), not only that a passage is linked, and approves or corrects it; values without a clear source are entered by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Event details sit in free-text notes.

steps.what: Clinical research coordinator confers with the investigator regarding seriousness, causality and reporting of events
Clinical research coordinator prepares the serious adverse event report
Investigator checks the final event report, its event details, seriousness and causality, and signs it
Clinical research coordinator submits the signed report to the ethics committee and oversight agencies
Clinical research coordinator tracks reporting deadlines and follow-up reports

approvals.approved_version: The serious adverse event report exactly as checked and signed by the investigator in s5, submitted once to the ethics committee and the oversight agencies this study reports to; any change needs a new check and signature.

tasks.design: The data capture tool proposes adverse event form values from the medical record, each linked to its source passage, and the coordinator approves or corrects each one. Seriousness and causality stay with the investigator. The report form fills from the approved case report form, the investigator signs, and the coordinator submits. A register computes reporting deadlines from the event date and seriousness and reminds the coordinator of follow-up reports.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event details were copied from notes into forms and reports, and deadlines tracked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Data capture tools that propose form values from source documents with approval per value.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether an event is related to the study drug.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the full story of a side effect from a patient.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and deadline tracking; judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive complete and on time.

evidence.claim: A data capture tool proposes case report form values from source documents; a person approves each.
Serious adverse events in trials must be reported to the ethics committee within fixed deadlines.

assumptions: Boundary: from collecting an event to the submitted report and follow-ups; the committee's assessment is outside.
Input contract for s2: source documents in the hospital record readable by the data capture tool for studies that have it, about 60% of studies; s2 is priced at that share.
Collection, conferring and submitting keep their full time; the investigator's time is outside the coordinator's savings.
unknowns: Which studies use a data capture tool with source proposals.
research_questions: Are reporting deadlines missed less often?

already_counted.description: Clinical research coordinator approves or corrects proposed values.

incremental.description: Clinical research coordinator sets deadline rules per study.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the record is readable by the tool in only a third of studies, so s2 keeps 80 (12.6); high: about 60% of studies have the tool as assumed (17.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor study activities: check visits against the protocol schedule, review source documents against forms, track amendments, training and delegation, and discuss deviations with the investigator to ensure compliance with protocols and policies.

steps.what: Clinical research coordinator checks study visits and procedures against the protocol schedule
Clinical research coordinator reviews source documents against case report forms
Clinical research coordinator tracks protocol amendments, staff training and the delegation log
Study staff confirm reading each new protocol version in the site file
Clinical research coordinator discusses deviations with the investigator

tasks.design: The data capture tool computes each participant's visit windows from the protocol schedule and lists visits that are due, missed or out of window, from the visit dates study staff enter. The electronic site file keeps protocol versions with read receipts for each staff member and the delegation log with training dates, and flags staff working on a version they have not read. Source verification and handling deviations stay with the coordinator and investigator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visit windows and training were tracked in spreadsheets and paper site files.
tasks.enabler_now: Data capture tools with visit schedules and electronic site files with read receipts.
tasks.still_hard: Deviations that only show in the clinical notes.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which deviation puts a patient at risk.
tasks.altitude: Less tracking by hand; compliance judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether monitoring visits find fewer missed windows.

evidence.claim: A policy tool keeps a versioned library with multi-stage approvals and maps documents to rules.
Records apps with versions, read receipts and review dates replace spreadsheets and mail-outs.
Systems that monitor staff need works council consent; read receipts are used for compliance, not ratings.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring a study at the site; sponsor monitoring is outside.
Input contract for s1: visit dates entered by study staff in the data capture tool at each visit.
Input contract for s3: protocol versions uploaded by the coordinator and read receipts given by staff in the site file (s5, share 1).
Discussing deviations keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of studies with electronic site files.

incremental.description: Clinical research coordinator enters the protocol schedule for each new study and amendment in the data capture tool.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: visit dates are often entered late, so the coordinator still checks many visits by hand and s1 keeps 70, and staff skip read receipts, so s3 keeps 80 (11.9); high: visit windows and read receipts used as designed (21.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Screen candidates for subject enrollment, attend the consent conversation, check that informed consent is properly obtained and documented, and register enrolment.

steps.what: Clinical research coordinator screens candidates against inclusion and exclusion criteria
Clinical research coordinator attends the consent conversation and gives time to consider
Clinical research coordinator checks that informed consent is properly documented: version, signatures and dates
Clinical research coordinator registers enrolment: typed in the study database and again in the hospital record today, entered once in the study database after the change
Clinical research coordinator checks the enrolment before it goes to the hospital record: patient, study, consent version and date
Clinical research coordinator releases the checked enrolment to set the study flag in the hospital record

tasks.design: A saved query in the hospital record lists patients who meet the coded criteria, and the coordinator and investigator decide who is approached; no one is included by the query alone. The consent conversation stays human. In the electronic site file the consent form is checked against the current approved version, with required signature and date fields. Enrolment is entered once in the study database; after the coordinator checks it, the coordinator releases it and the integration sets the study flag in the hospital record.

approvals.approved_version: The enrolment of this patient in this study, with consent version and date exactly as checked by the coordinator in s4b, sent once to set the study flag in this patient's hospital record; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Candidates were found by reading clinic lists, and enrolment was entered in two systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved record queries, electronic site files and links between study database and hospital record.
tasks.still_hard: Criteria that are not coded in the record.
tasks.human_edge: Making sure a patient truly understands before signing.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and double entry; consent stays human.

reach.learn: Whether more eligible patients are found.

evidence.claim: Decisions must not rest on automation alone without human intervention and a right to contest.
Coded record queries can list patients meeting structured criteria.

assumptions: Boundary: from screening to registered enrolment; study visits are outside.
Input contract for s1: diagnoses, lab values and medication coded in the hospital record, covering about half the criteria; the rest are checked by reading the record.
Input contract for s4: the study database linked to the hospital record by the hospital data team.

The consent conversation keeps its full time. s3 keeps 80: the site file checks the form version and required fields, but the coordinator still reads every signature and date. s4 keeps 60 because the second entry in the hospital record drops but entering the study database stays.
unknowns: Share of criteria that are coded.

already_counted.description: Clinical research coordinator checks query hits against the full record.

incremental.description: Clinical research coordinator sets up the query per study with the data team.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few criteria are coded, so s1 keeps 85, and the integration is not live, so enrolment is still typed twice and s4 keeps 90 (9.5); high: about half the criteria coded and the integration live as designed (20.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
